newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA cargo services at Paris/CDG normal.
newsitem.headline: BA cargo services at Paris/CDG normal.

text.p: BA World Cargo said it was maintaining a normal service at Paris/Charles de Gaulle airport despite disruption to its passenger services as a result of the UK airline's bid to obtain tighter security at France's biggest airport.

BA has been closing its counters at CDG for several hours a day since the weekend after Air Algerie, state airline of violence-torn Algeria, resumed flights, after a two-year break, opening check-in desks next to the UK carrier.
"There has been no impact on freight because shipments are not in the same building as those of Air Algerie," a Paris-based BA Cargo official told Reuters.

On Tuesday in a statement BA director Europe, George Cooper, said the airline was thinking of moving its entire operation - up to 60 services a day involving 60,000 passengers - to Paris' other major airport, at Orly, unless security demands were met.

"If the decision was taken to move to Orly it would not be too problematical for freight in that we would not be starting from scratch as we already load shipments on to our daily Boeing 767 service from the airport to London," the official said.

BA's CDG handling agent, France Handling, had a branch office at Orly whose facilities the airline used in loading Beaujolais shipments on to two 747 passenger flights last November, the official added.

"Obviously, most of our forwarder customers are at CDG so us being Orly-based would mean some logistics adjustment but nothing of a major nature. Truck services from the north would take a little longer to arrive given Orly's location south of Paris but by the same token transit time for truck services from southern French cities would be shortened."
BA's French subsidiaries, TAT European Airlines and Air Liberte are based at Orly.

The official added that one example of Orly's "workability" as a freight gateway came from American Airlines - a major carrier of belly-hold cargo - which had been based there for some time despite most of the Paris air cargo community being headquartered at CDG.
